paper.title: A conversion theorem and minimax optimality for continuum contextual bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual continuum bandits, general class F' with gamma-Hölder dependence on context (conversion theorem)
unmapped: Fixed unknown function f(x,c); contexts c_t in [0,1]^p chosen by an adaptive adversary
f(x,.) is gamma-Hölder in context with constant L (Assumption 1)
f(.,c) belongs to a generic class F' for which an input algorithm has static regret <= F(T)F_1(T)
Contextual regret compares to per-round minimizer of f(.,c_t)
Choice of K in eq. (Kvalue) uses L, p, d, tau's
settings.definition_quote: Let $\com\subseteq \mathbb{R}^{\dx}$ be a convex body. Let $f:\mathbb{R}^{\dx}\times [0,1]^{\dc}\to\mathbb{R}$ be an unknown function. At each round $t$: A context $\bc_t\in [0,1]^{\dc}$ is revealed by the adversary. ... the learner chooses a query point $\bz_t\in\com$ and gets a noisy evaluation of $f(\bz_t,\bc_t)$

unmapped: Action set is the hypercube [0,1]^d
f(x,.) gamma-Hölder in context with constant L
Contexts adversarial in [0,1]^p; contextual regret against per-round minimizer
settings.definition_quote: Assume that $\com = [0,1]^{\dx}$ and that the observations in \eqref{eq:observe} are noise-free ... $|f(\bx,\bc) - f(\bx',\bc)|\leq \Lc'\norm{\bx-\bx'}$

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual convex bandits with sub-Gaussian noise
unmapped: f(.,c) convex for every context (convex not in function_class vocabulary)
f(x,.) gamma-Hölder in context with constant L
Contexts adversarial; contextual regret
settings.definition_quote: Let $\mathcal{F}$ be the set of functions $f$ such that $f(\cdot,\bc)$ is convex for all $\bc\in[0,1]^{\dc}$. Assume that, conditionally on the past observations, $\xi_t$ ... is a zero-mean $\sigma$-sub-Gaussian random variable

settings.name_in_paper: Bandit optimization of strongly convex and smooth functions f(.,c_t) with noisy evaluations (static regret)
unmapped: Loss sequence f(.,c_t) with c_t arbitrary (adversarial sequence of functions from a fixed family)
max_{x in K}|f(x,c)| <= M, M known to learner
Strong convexity and smoothness hold on all of R^d
Noise sigma-sub-Gaussian and independent of algorithm randomization; not assumed mutually independent
Learner uses a mu-self-concordant barrier on K
settings.definition_quote: For $(\alpha,\Lx,M)\in (0,\infty)\times[\alpha,\infty)\times(0,\infty)$, we assume that $f\in \mathcal{F}_{\alpha,\Lx}(M)$ ... i) $f(\cdot,\bc)$ is $\alpha$-strongly convex. ii) $f(\cdot,\bc)$ is $\Lx$-smooth. iii) $\max_{\bx\in\com}|f(\bx,\bc)|\leq M$.

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual bandits with strongly convex and smooth functions, sub-Gaussian noise
unmapped: f(x,.) gamma-Hölder in context with constant L (used to tune K)
|f| <= M on K, M known

source.quote: For $(\alpha,\Lx,M, \gamma,\Lc)\in (0,\infty)\times [3\alpha,\infty)\times [\alpha+1,\infty)\times[0,1]\times [0,\infty)$ consider the class ... Let $\com = B^d$ ... Let $\pi\in\Pi$ be any randomized procedure ... Then, \sup_{f\in\bar{\mathcal{F}}}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\Exp\left[f(\bz_t,\bc_t) - \min_{\bz\in\com}f(\bz,\bc_t)\right]\geq \cst\left(\min\left(1, \Lc^{\frac{2(\dc+\gamma)}{\dc+2\gamma}}\right)T^{\frac{\dc+\gamma}{\dc+2\gamma}}+\min\left(T,\dx \sqrt{T}\right)\right)

results.notes: Constant independent of d, p, T. With gamma=0 (class F_0(L)) gives linear regret. Holds also for algorithms querying outside K and extends to any convex body; also a lower bound for convex contextual bandits. Noise recorded as Gaussian (a special case satisfying the condition).
